# orangu

> orangu is local, offline, deterministic observability for coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, Cowork
> and Desktop). The orangu 0.8.0 CLI reads the `.jsonl` transcripts that are already on your disk.
> It turns them into a self-contained HTML report, a stable JSON API, cross-session aggregates, and a
> harness report. The harness report compares what your config declares with what your sessions used.
> Optional Claude Code skills turn that evidence into reviewable proposals and receipts. The loop is
> observe, see, improve.

Concretely, you can:

- `npx orangu` : opens a menu in the terminal. Choose this repository, all sessions, or one session. In a pipe or in CI, it prints a short summary of the latest session.
- `npx orangu report` : builds and opens a self-contained HTML report for the latest session. `orangu report <id>` opens another session, and `orangu report current` opens the current Claude Code session.
- `npx orangu serve` : opens a live viewer on loopback (127.0.0.1) over every local session.
- `npx orangu repo` / `npx orangu global` : aggregates every session of one repository, or of the whole machine.
- `npx orangu harness` : compares the declared skills, MCP servers, agents and hooks with what sessions used or left idle, in tokens.
- `npx orangu analyze <id> --json` : prints the full analysis object. `--slim` prints the projection that LLM consumers read.
- `npx orangu pick` : lists the sessions, the running ones first, and opens the report of the one you choose.
- `npx orangu list` / `watch` : list the sessions, or tail a live session.
- `npx orangu evidence` / `estimate` : give bounded evidence to skills, or size what an LLM would read.
- `npx orangu suggest` / `feedback` : read and write the suggestion records in `~/.orangu`, or open a localhost feedback form.
- In Claude Code, after `/plugin marketplace add NissanOhana/orangu` and `/plugin install orangu`: `/orangu:analyze`, `/orangu:improve latest`, `/orangu:apply <sg_id>`, `/orangu:harness`, `/orangu:show-me latest` (a slide deck and a written report, as offline HTML), `/orangu:feedback`.

Facts an LLM should not get wrong:

- Tokens only. orangu never converts tokens into any other unit: no rates, no estimates in another unit, nothing with a symbol in front of it. Input, cache-read, cache-write and output tokens are its only usage metric because they are the only one the transcript records.
- No model in the measurement path. Parsing, redaction, counting, reconciliation, matching and ranking are plain code. The same transcript in gives byte-identical analysis out.
- Reports make zero network requests and ship `default-src 'none'`. orangu uploads nothing. There is no account, proxy, instrumentation, or telemetry.
- Redaction is on by default. Shareable output omits prompt and result text unless you ask for `--include-text`.
- Skills read `orangu ... --json` / `orangu evidence`, never the raw `.jsonl`.
- orangu never applies a proposal automatically. `/orangu:apply` runs only on an explicitly reviewed session or repo proposal. Global (whole-harness) proposals are review-only.
- orangu reports quality, time and tokens as separate axes. There is no composite score.
- orangu reads history retroactively. It can analyze every session on your disk from the minute you install it.

- [README](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/README.md): what it is, quick start, design principles, positioning.
- [Usage](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md): every command, report and app surfaces, supported inputs and limits.
- [Determinism and skill authority](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/docs/DETERMINISM.md): which layer owns evidence, proposals, application and verification.
- [Privacy](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md): what stays local, what redaction removes, what to check before sharing.
- [Data contracts](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/docs/DATA-CONTRACTS.md): Analysis, evidence, proposal and receipt shapes.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): pipeline, modules, build and correctness gates.
- [Skills](https://github.com/NissanOhana/orangu/tree/main/plugin/skills): the shipped Claude Code skill instructions.

## Getting started

- orangu needs Node.js 20 or newer. It has zero runtime dependencies.
- `npx orangu` opens a menu: this repository, all sessions, or one session. In a pipe or in CI, it prints a short summary of the latest session. `npx orangu report` opens the latest local session. `npx orangu serve` follows all of them live.
- Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add NissanOhana/orangu` then `/plugin install orangu`.
- [Sample report](https://nissanohana.github.io/orangu/sample.html): a synthetic, deterministic report you can open without installing anything.
- [Repository sample](https://nissanohana.github.io/orangu/sample-repo.html): the same synthetic corpus aggregated across sessions, as `npx orangu repo --html` writes it.
